title: Preserve escape sequences across streaming frames and sanitize function-call payloads for OpenAI compatibility
author: Sofia Martinez
description: Motivation: streaming responses that include escape sequences (e.g. "\n", backslash-escaped JSON fragments, or grammar escape tokens) were intermittently split across stream frames which caused downstream constrained decoders (CFG/regex backends) and the OpenAI compatibility function_call deserializer to mis-parse structured outputs. This PR implements a streaming-side preservation layer that: 1) tracks incomplete escape sequences across frame boundaries, 2) emits framing metadata so the constrained-decoder shims can reconstitute tokenized escape atoms, and 3) applies a sanitizer step for function_call payloads produced by the OpenAI compatibility layer to ensure tool/callee names and JSON args are valid and well-quoted. Changes in this PR: - Streaming runtime: buffer-aware escape preservation that patches split backslash/quote sequences across chunks. This is low-overhead and only activates when we detect an open escape/token boundary. - OpenAI compat: function_call sanitizer that validates JSON payloads, coerces single quotes into double quotes where safe, and rejects ambiguous truncated unicode escapes; adds a soft-fallback that rewrites to a safe literal when aggressive repairs would risk changing semantics. - Constraint backends: small adapter for CFG and regex backends to consume the new framing metadata and to treat reassembled escape atoms as single lexical tokens for constraint matching. - Tokenizer edgecases: fixes for UTF-8 continuation bytes that were treated as separate tokens in some quantized tokenizers, plus additional normalization for byte-pair splits at backslashes. - Tests: new unit tests exercising split-escape streaming, regression tests with real-world tool names and nested JSON args, and fuzz harness additions to the end-to-end openai-compat path. - Docs: short note in streaming.md and openai-compat.md describing the framing metadata and sanitizer semantics. Checklist: - [x] Add streaming buffer logic and unit tests - [x] Add function_call sanitizer and integration tests - [x] Add decoder adapter for framing metadata - [x] Add tokenizer normalization tests and fuzz harness - [x] Update docs and changelog Impact: This resolves multiple customer-facing incidents where structured outputs used in downstream tool calls were rejected or mangled. The sanitizer is intentionally conservative; any payloads that cannot be safely repaired will surface as structured-repair-needed events in the logs so customers can inspect and opt-in to more aggressive repairs. Related work: ENG-4821 streaming stability spike, ENG-4899 openai compat edgecases, SUP-1182 customer report (function calls failing for escaped JSON).

e5c7a89: constraint-adapter: consume framing metadata and treat reassembled atoms as tokens
d2f9cbb: tokenizer: normalize backslash splits and utf8 continuation handling
a7c1e13: tests: split-escape unit tests + integration fixtures
review_thread: Ethan Cho: Please add a benchmark for the no-op path to prove the overhead is negligible. Response: added microbenchmark and numbers to the PR description (see streaming perf comment).

Priya Raman: The sanitizer looks strong, but we should avoid throwing 4xx to customers when we can fallback. Can we add a telemetry event? Response: added a structured 'structured-repair-needed' event and documented it.

Liam O'Connor: Edgecase: unicode escape like \uD83D split across token boundary could be mangled. Fix? Response: updated tokenizer normalizer to detect surrogate pair splits and avoid in-place repair; prefer log + markup for operator review.
ci_summary: Initial CI had a flaky streaming integration test failure (race on buffer GC); fixed by adding an await in the test harness. Full CI now green: unit tests, integration, lint, and fuzz. Fuzz harness run found two minor tokenizer regressions which were corrected.
release_notes: Streaming: preserve escape sequences across frames to improve structured-output stability; OpenAI compatibility: function_call payload sanitizer to reduce malformed tool calls. No breaking changes. Customers may see structured-repair-needed telemetry for ambiguous payloads.
notes_for_backport: Patch is small and should be cherry-picked to release/2026-02 for customers on managed "legacy-streaming". Watch for tokenizer ABI differences across release branches.
testing_instructions: Run unit tests: cargo test -p streaming --release. Run integration: ./scripts/run_integration.sh tests/integration/openai_compat/split_escape.jsonl. Fuzz: ./scripts/fuzz_runner --target openai_compat. Check logs for 'structured-repair-needed' events during integration.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: changes are localized to streaming and openai-compat shims. The sanitizer is conservative and defaults to logging rather than hard rejects. Performance overhead measured at ~0.3% p50 token latency in microbenchmarks when active; no measurable overhead on typical samples where escape preservation is not triggered.
author_signoff: Sofia Martinez: Implemented and ran full CI, validated with e2e fixtures and customer repros. Will monitor telemetry for the next 2 weeks post-merge.
changelog_entry: fix(streaming): preserve split escape sequences across stream frames; feat(openai-compat): function_call payload sanitizer and constrained-decoder framing adapter
